title: Finite presentation transfers from a finite type subring
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $M$ be an $S$-module. If $S$ is of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $M$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], then $M$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561 (lemma-finitely-presented-over-subring), statement and proof

proof.text: By the finite-type hypothesis, choose n and a surjective R-algebra map R[x_1, ..., x_n] to S. By finite presentation of M over R, choose R-generators y_1, ..., y_m and finitely many relation vectors (a_{i1}, ..., a_{im}) generating the kernel of R^m to M.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: “We may assume S = R[x_1, ..., x_n]/J” through the choice of generators and relations

proof.text: For every i,j, express x_i y_j as an R-linear combination sum_k a_{ijk} y_k. Let N be the S-module on generators y_1, ..., y_m with the finitely many R-relation vectors and the nm action relations x_i y_j = sum_k a_{ijk} y_k. Thus N has a presentation S^{t+nm} to S^m to N to 0, so N is finitely presented as an S-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph constructing N and its finite presentation

proof.text: The assignment of the generators of N to the corresponding elements y_j of M respects all defining relations, and the y_j generate M as an R-module, hence as an S-module. It therefore induces a surjective S-linear map phi:N to M.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: “By construction there is a surjective map phi : N to M.”

proof.text: Every element of N is represented by polynomial coefficients in the x_i. Applying the action relations lowers the total polynomial degree one monomial at a time, so the polynomial reduces inductively to an R-linear combination of the generators; this is exactly the polynomial-action reduction lemma. If such a reduced combination maps to zero in M, its coefficient vector lies in the R-span of the chosen relation vectors, which are also defining relations in N. Hence ker(phi)=0.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph beginning “Suppose z = ...” through the conclusion that phi is injective

proof.text: The map phi is therefore an isomorphism, and the finite presentation of N over S transfers to M.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, end of proof
